newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dornbusch says peso should be 20 pct lower - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dornbusch says peso should be 20 pct lower - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Institute of Technology economics guru Rudiger Dornbusch said the peso should be 20 percent lower than current levels at around nine pesos per dollar, Mexico City daily reported Wednesday.

Citing the man who correctly predicted the 1994 December devaluation in an article datelined from New York, Reforma said Dornbush continued to disagree with the monetary policies of Mexico's central bank and said the Mexican economy can only grow via increased exports.
Dornbusch said that if the Banco de Mexico did not "correct" policies in coming months, problems of the past could be repeated, Reforma said.
The economist added that former Finance Minister Pedro Aspe was the best option to relieve current Banco de Mexico governor Miguel Mancera when his governership ends January 1, 1998.

Dornbusch's recent criticism of the Banco de Mexico and comments about the peso's relative strength against the dollar were partly blamed by foreign exchange traders for an abrupt weakening of the peso two weeks after a long period of stability.
